director.chapterArc: A tense interrogation that shifts from personal vengeance to tactical necessity, culminating in Rook's brutal honesty about his own nature.
director.restraintNote: The scene is driven by the contrast between the knife at Tull's throat and the sudden shout of danger. The emotional core is not anger but a cold realization: action precedes thought. Maintain distance; let the violence feel clinical, then shift to Rook's exhausted confession.

cues.delivery: Tull speaks with the flat affect of a man finishing business. No self-pity; just facts.
cues.from: "Then you know it's on a table at Barrow Gate and it's been on a table somewhere for nineteen years, and I've never once hidden it, and a man who's been looking for me for eleven years has been looking for me poorly." He lay still under the knee on his chest. He did not thrash, and he did not beg, and he spoke like a man conducting the last piece of business in a long day. "Homura. That's the valley up north with the wire round it."
cues.through: "That was a contract and it was a bad one and I was paid for it, and I'm not going to tell you it wasn't me, because you've got me on a road and you'd not believe me and I'd only be dying with a lie in my mouth." He moved his head slightly. "I don't remember you. I want that said. You're in front of me with a face like the end of the world and I'd not know you from a gatepost, and I've had eleven years of my life since then, and that's the truth of it and you can do what you like with it."

cues.delivery: Rook counts the past with precision. The number 'Nine' is a hard pivot point.
cues.reason: Narrative shift to Rook's internal realization.

cues.delivery: The mention of 'Lowry Bend' triggers a physical reaction in Tull; the narrator must pause to let that shift land.
cues.from: "Nine years ago, in the autumn, a company took a defence contract at a village four hundred miles south of here on the edge of a fracture. Three lines out past a mill on the second night. The north line."
cues.reason: Subtext: The specific location changes the dynamic from general revenge to personal history.

cues.delivery: Rook lists his dead family. The tone is not weeping; it is a heavy inventory of loss.
cues.from: "My mother," said Rook. "And Arn. And Tobin."
cues.through: "Well. There it is, then. I'd wondered what it was. Six years of a man buying our brass in every wall on the coast." He looked up. "Go on. I'd rather it was for the lane than for the valley, if it's all the same to you. The valley was work. The lane was me being told a wrong thing and believing it, which is what a man's actually made of."

cues.delivery: The knife action is described with clinical detachment. The pause at 'one second' must feel elongated.
cues.from: The knife came out of Rook's coat and went in under the man's jaw.
cues.through: The knife did not come out. It went in a little further. There was a second, one whole second, in which Toren was entirely certain he was about to watch a man die on a road, and in which the man on the ground was entirely certain of it too, and had shut his eyes and stopped talking and gone still in the way that people do.
cues.reason: Narrative focus on the physical reality of violence.

cues.delivery: Rook's command to Tull is a statement. The transition from killing to releasing requires no emotional swing.
cues.from: "Get up," said Rook, "and walk in front of me, and if any man of yours comes forward before I'm across that arch I will put this through your kidney and neither of us will care by then whose fault it was."
cues.reason: Character voice for Rook's tactical decision.

cues.delivery: The description of the barrier is physical and strange. The command to Toren must be urgent but not panicked.
cues.from: Then the air across the neck of the arch went the way air goes over a fire, a sort of leaning, and something came up between his hands and stood there — not a wall, not a light, nothing you could point at and describe to somebody who had not seen it. A twelve-foot span of brick with something across it. It was the thing he had watched a man do in a road cut on the first day of everything, and again on a bridge in the fog, and it was the thing that same man had told them all four nights ago on a dark verge that he could not do this week, in advance, in daylight, so that nobody would be carrying a picture of it.

cues.delivery: The combat sequence is staccato. Toren's scream and Rook's stillness must contrast sharply.
cues.from: He ran the two hundred feet of road bed north with the cart coming up out of the dark in front of him and Dessa's voice going steadily over the top of everything — two at the wheel, one behind you Wyck, he's on your left and he's low — and Wyck Tanner standing across the neck of the road in front of a cart with a dead boy in it, with the bar in both hands and his left arm bent the wrong way at the wrist, hitting men.
cues.through: The spear went into him high in the back, through the meat above the shoulder blade on the left side, hard enough to move him six inches forward on his feet, and he made a sound Toren had never heard out of him and did not lift his hands, and the thing across the arch did not go out.
cues.reason: Narrative focus on the climax of action.

cues.delivery: Rook's account is delivered with exhaustion. Senna's interruption must cut through the silence.
cues.through: "I should think so," said Senna Voss, from the cart, in a voice like a dry stick breaking. "I'd have been very annoyed to be carried over an arch by a lot of children and then wasted."
cues.reason: Character voice for Rook and Senna.

cues.delivery: Rook's final explanation is a revelation of his own nature. The tone must be flat and honest.
cues.through: "Don't ask me today whether I'd do it again," he said. "Ask me in about a year. I'll answer it then, and you'll be old enough to hear whatever it turns out to be."

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the name as a confrontation begins.

He moved his head slightly. "I don't remember you. I want that said. You're in front of me with a face like the end of the world and I'd not know you from a gatepost, and I've had eleven years of my life since then, and that's the truth of it and you can do what you like with it."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after Tull's confession of memory loss.

pauses.after: "There were eleven of us in the long room and a girl held the door and got nine of us past you, and you stood outside it and counted, and you got to nine, and then you went round the back." Rook's voice had not risen once. "I was the fourth. You looked at me. You looked at every single one of us, because you were counting, and you have looked me in the face from four feet and you do not know me from a gatepost."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the realization that Rook was counted and ignored for years.

pauses.after: "Nine years ago, in the autumn, a company took a defence contract at a village four hundred miles south of here on the edge of a fracture. Three lines out past a mill on the second night. The north line."
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause to let 'Lowry Bend' register as a specific threat.
Contrast: Tull does not feel remorse.
Speaker reset after Tull's shift in tone from defensive to resigned.
Emphasis on the sound of realization and acceptance.
Preparation for the violent action that follows.

pauses.after: Rook did not move for one second.
pauses.reason: Scene break; the knife goes in and then stops. A long beat for the tension of death.
Speaker reset after Rook's command to Tull.
Clarification of the magical effect's nature.

pauses.after: Rook did not turn round and did not lift his hands.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause before the spear strike lands on Rook.

pauses.after: They did it in order, the way they had come off the road the morning before: the wounded first, and two of them walking backward, and a voice down there counting people into the boats; and the last thing Toren saw of Cinder Company on the Level was a big man in a good coat standing on the bank at the bottom of the slope with his hands at his sides, looking up at the arch for about four seconds before he turned round and followed them into the reeds.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset after the enemy retreats and Tull is released.
Contrast to the expected heroism of a dying man.

pauses.after: "And what I had left after that was about enough for one thing, and the one thing was either the last two seconds of him or twelve feet of arch, and I have spent eleven years telling myself I'd know which way I'd go and I did not know. I was not certain until my hands moved."
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause before Rook begins his 'bill' of costs.
Emphasis on Rook's agency in letting Tull go.
Speaker reset after Toren's question about the release of Tull.
